title: SilverLake pilot: activation matrix + tenant affinity — slot booking request
text:
SilverLake pilot: activation matrix + tenant affinity — slot booking request

['From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@silverlake.ai>\\nTo: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>\\nCc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>\\nDate: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700\\nSubject: New: Activation matrix + tenant affinity for SilverLake pilot\\n\\nIrene / Tessa / Marissa —\\n\\nThanks again for the demo yesterday. SilverLake’s pilot steering committee reviewed the flow and they’ve asked for two items to be in the pilot acceptance criteria before we sign the PO: 1) an \\"activation matrix\\" that lets us map model behavior to tenant activation tiers (free / standard / enterprise) so we can enforce different generation limits & routing rules per tier, and 2) a tenant affinity mechanism so requests from high-value tenants are routed to a dedicated warm pool (or pinned model variant) to guarantee sub-200ms tail latency for our premium customers.\\n\\nI’ve attached a short SOW excerpt and a rough activation spreadsheet (activation-matrix-proposal.xlsx) to show the ask. High level timeline expectations from SilverLake: pilot kickoff by May 10, acceptance gates by end of June.\\n\\nCan Redwood commit to blocking a sprint slot to implement a minimal activation matrix + tenant affinity (even as a config/flag) for pilot? If not, what is the earliest alternate path — e.g., config-based routing + pre-warm shim?\\n\\nPriya\\nHead of Product Partnerships\\nSilverLake AI\\n\\n--\\nAttachment: SL_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf, 42KB)\\nAttachment: activation-matrix-proposal.xlsx (xlsx, 18KB)', 'From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>\\nTo: Priya Rao <priya.rao@silverlake.ai>\\nCc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>\\nDate: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: New: Activation matrix + tenant affinity for SilverLake pilot\\n\\nPriya —\\n\\nReally appreciate the clarity. Short answer: we can get you a pragmatic path, but I need to loop in Product + Eng to confirm scope/ETA for the pilot window. Irene, Marissa — can you weigh in on whether Product can prioritize a minimal activation matrix (mapping tiers to routing & limits) and an affinity toggle that pins VIP tenant traffic to a warm pool? The ask is gated by the PO timing; SilverLake wants pilot-ready controls before signing.\\n\\nIf Product/Eng can’t ship everything by early May, we should propose a hybrid acceptance: config-level routing + a pre-warm policy (short-term) with a roadmap commit for full matrix support before the end of June.\\n\\nTessa\\nAccount Exec — Strategic Customers\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\n', 'From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>\\nTo: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>\\nCc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>\\nDate: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 09:47:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: New: Activation matrix + tenant affinity for SilverLake pilot\\n\\nThanks for looping me in. Quick product read: 1) Activation matrix = mapping \\"tenant tier\\" -> {model variant, rate limits, routing priority, cache TTLs}. 2) Tenant affinity = sticky routing to a warm pool or reserved instance set. Both are doable, but with different effort levels.\\n\\nOptions (tradeoffs):\\n- Minimal config-driven approach (LOW effort, shipable as an API + Console toggle): let Sales attach metadata to the account and route by simple rules. No per-tenant warm-pool guarantee, but we can implement priority queuing and pre-warm triggers. ETA: 3 weeks (can align to pilot start if we slot it now).\\n- Medium scope: config + lightweight warm pool affinity (pin tenant to a small reserved pool on demand). Requires capacity planning changes and autoscaler hooks. ETA: 6–8 weeks.\\n- Full scope: activation matrix + routing engine + console management + analytics. ETA: 12+ weeks.\\n\\nDev — do you see any blockers to a 3-week delivery if we scope this as config + pre-warm hooks (no hard affinity guarantees)? Also, we’ll want to draft acceptance criteria and a canary plan. I added a link to a short spec template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bSL-Activation-Proposal\\n\\nNeha\\nDirector, Product Management\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\n', 'From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>\\nTo: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>\\nCc: \\nDate: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 13:15:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: New: Activation matrix + tenant affinity for SilverLake pilot\\n\\nThanks — technical quick-take. The minimal config + pre-warm hooks is the safest path to hit the May 10 pilot kickoff. Implementation notes:\\n- Add a per-account metadata field (tenant_tier) consumed by the routing layer.\\n- Implement routing rule precedence: tenant_tier -> route to (shared pool | priority queue | reserved pool).\\n- Pre-warm trigger: when tenant_tier==enterprise, trigger a short-lived pinned instance and pre-populate KV cache for frequent prefixes. This is a stop-gap; it reduces tail latency but doesn’t offer strict SLAs.\\n\\nEstimated work: 3 backend engineer-weeks + 1 infra week for temporary reserved pool orchestration + small Console work to expose a toggle. If Product signs off on the acceptance criteria and we get a sprint slot in April, we can deliver the minimal approach by May 6 (internal canary by May 3).\\n\\nRisk: capacity contention during heavy global traffic windows — we need a fallback policy to avoid impacting other customers. Suggest we include a safe fallback config in the acceptance criteria.\\n\\nDev\\nSenior Software Engineer — Serving Runtime\\n\\nAttachment: sequence-log-sample.txt (txt, 2KB)', "From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>\\nTo: Priya Rao <priya.rao@silverlake.ai>\\nCc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, procurement@silverlake.ai\\nDate: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 18:03:00 -0700\\nSubject: Re: SilverLake pilot: activation matrix + tenant affinity — slot booking request\\n\\nPriya —\\n\\nGood news: Product and Eng have proposed a pragmatic path we can slot in April to meet a May 6 delivery for the minimal acceptance bundle (config-driven activation matrix + pre-warm trigger). Key points:\\n- Redwood will deliver the config API + Console toggle and the pre-warm hook by May 6, with an internal canary May 3.\\n- This is explicitly a pilot-scoped capability: it provides priority routing and pre-warm behavior but does not provide firm latency SLAs for all edge cases. We will add a full affinity/reservation feature in the Q3 roadmap (ETA end of June for a stronger affinity implementation).\\n- Acceptance criteria: (1) ability to set tenant_tier per account; (2) routed requests for tier=enterprise hit the pre-warm path 90% of the time in canary; (3) documented fallback behavior under capacity pressure.\\n\\nNext steps: Irene — can you please confirm we can include this acceptance wording in the SOW so SilverLake can move the PO forward? Priya / Procurement — if this scope is acceptable I’ll ask Legal to add the pilot acceptance gates to the SOW and propose a delivery milestone.\\n\\nTessa\\nAccount Exec — Strategic Customers\\nRedwood Inference\\n\\nOn Apr 6, 2027, 09:47, Priya Rao <priya.rao@silverlake.ai> wrote:\\n> Tessa / Irene —\\n>\\n> Thank you. The pilot-scoped definition looks good in principle. SilverLake’s engineering lead asked for a HW/instance cap on the pre-warm pool (we'll need to see numbers during canary) and explicit fallback language so we can manage customer expectations.\\n>\\n> We’re happy to accept the pilot deliverable if the SOW includes those points and we get the canary data to sign off. Can you push the updated SOW draft (with acceptance wording and fallback limits) by next Monday?\\n>\\n> Priya\\n> Head of Product Partnerships\\n> SilverLake AI\\n\\n--\\nRelated Link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/SL-2027-0421\\n"]
